title: Minestrone
subtitle: Italian vegetable and pasta soup
excerpt: A thick Italian vegetable soup with cannellini beans, seasonal vegetables, and small pasta. Every Italian region has a version; this is the core idea, whatever vegetables are to hand, cooked slowly with tomato, garlic, and a parmesan rind.

recipe.sourceNotes: Minestrone means simply 'big soup' in Italian, from minestra (soup) with the augmentative suffix. It has no single canonical recipe and varies entirely by region and season. The Ligurian version includes pesto stirred in at the end; the Milanese version uses rice instead of pasta; the southern version uses different beans. This recipe gives a flexible base that works year-round.

content.text: The best minestrone is made with a parmesan rind simmered in the pot from the start. If you have one, drop it in when you add the stock, it dissolves slowly and adds a savoury depth that no other ingredient replicates. Keep a bag of rinds in the freezer for exactly this purpose. The soup should be thick enough that a spoon leaves a trail through it.

items.preparation: grated, plus a rind if available

content.text: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, celery, and carrot for 10 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 2 minutes.

Add the courgette, potato, and green beans. Stir and cook for 3 minutes. Add the tinned tomatoes, stock, and parmesan rind if using. Season with salt and pepper. Bring to a simmer and cook, partially covered, for 25 minutes.
Add the cannellini beans and pasta. Cook for a further 12 minutes until the pasta is tender. Remove the parmesan rind.
Taste for salt. Ladle into bowls, tear over the basil, and finish with plenty of grated parmesan and a drizzle of olive oil.
